description: With Saruman's deck, Glorfindel and a group of Hobbits travel into the civilized confines of Gondor, south of the White Mountains, to rally mannish factions against Sauron's hosts. The deck relies heavily on attack avoidance. The hazards mix is a pure Orc/Troll strategy.
strategy: Rely on attack avoidance (Concealment ×3, Stealth ×3, Dodge ×2) to move safely through Gondor. Glorfindel and the Hobbits form a light but mobile company. Keep Saruman at Isengard or send him to a faction site. Goal: play Gondor factions (Knights of Dol Amroth, Men of Anfalas/Anorien/Lebennin, Rangers of Ithilien) and major items (Palantir of Orthanc, Sapling of the White Tree, Scroll of Isildur). Dark Quarrels and Halfling Strength for emergency combat.

description: Elrond leads Alatar's companies into the Orc-holds of the mountains surrounding Rivendell. Their errand is to rescue Free People captives and recover stolen items. Gates of Morning and strong warriors see them through. The hazards feature a classic mix of corruption with Undead.
strategy: Core combo: Gates of Morning (×3) + The Cock Crows → combat bonus during the day. Play Rescue Prisoners in Orc-holds (Goblin Gate, Moria, Mount Gram, Mount Gundabad). Risky Blow + Many Turns and Doublings for aggressive combat. Elrond provides leadership bonus. Vilya as a major endgame score at Rivendell. Hazards: Undead (Barrow Wight, Slayer) combined with corruption (Lure of Expedience/Nature) to pressure the opponent.

description: With the prompting of Pallando, Thorin II leads a company of Dwarves into the Dragon lairs and Shadow-holds east of the Misty Mountains in a quest for their people. The Dwarves operate with a good mix of fighting enhancement and attack avoidance. The hazards are Animals and Wolves.
strategy: A Dwarf company under Thorin II operating in Dragon lairs and Shadow-holds east of the Misty Mountains. Not at Home (×2) + Concealment (×3) for attack avoidance. Iron Hill Dwarves and Men of Dorwinion as faction targets. Major items: Durin's Axe, The Arkenstone, and Thror's Map at The Lonely Mountain and Caves of Ulund. Bounty of the Hoard + Lucky Search for extra marshalling points. The Dwarves Are upon You (×2) as combat combo. Hazards: Animal threats (spiders, wolves) to pressure the opponent.

description: Along with Beorn, Gimli and Legolas, an unlikely duo of Dwarf and Elf, carry out missions of diplomacy in the hostile territories north of Mordor. Potent combat abilities with some subtle attack avoidance characterize these heroes of Radagast. The hazards feature ranks of roguish Men.
strategy: Run two companies: a Beorn group heading north and Gimli+Legolas heading east. Risky Blow (×3) for aggressive combat. New Friendship (×3) to play factions at unexpected locations. Noble Steed (×3) for extra movement. Goals: play Beornings, Easterlings, Wood Elves, Iron Hill Dwarves, and Men of Dorwinion. Vanishment as an escape route. Hazards: roguish Men (Lawless Men, Rank upon Rank, Sellswords Between Charters) to pressure the opponent.

description: Gandalf sends Aragorn and Arwen into the lands along the Anduin River to find lost icons of Gondor. Their efforts also take the pair to Minas Tirith to be crowned King and Queen. The deck relies primarily on attack avoidance. The hazards contain a heavy mix of good general creatures.
strategy: Core strategy: attack avoidance (Concealment ×3, Stealth ×3, Dodge ×2). Move Aragorn and Arwen to Minas Tirith for Return of the King as a major endgame score. Convert Beautiful Gold Ring (×3) into Lesser Ring or Magic Ring of Stealth. Noble Steed for fast movement along the Anduin. Rangers of Ithilien and Tower Guard of Minas Tirith as factions. Narsil as an item at Gondor sites. Hazards: a broad mix of Drakes and Men for wide coverage.

hazards.name: Ent in Search of the Entwives

description: Adunaphel sends traitorous bands bent upon thievery and espionage into the untainted domains of the Free Peoples. Her inherent knowledge of these areas provides some cover, but her missions are extremely difficult to carry out. The hazards feature a potent offering of Drakes.
strategy: A challenging Minion spy deck operating in Free Peoples' domains. A Nice Place to Hide (×3) + Not Slay Needlessly (×3) as core attack avoidance in Free-domains. Secrets of Their Forging + The Least of Gold Rings to obtain Dwarven Rings as major items. To Satisfy the Questioner + Tokens to Show for information marshalling points. Adunaphel's special ability provides knowledge of Free-domain routes. Hazards: Drakes (Cave/Marsh/Rain/True Fire Drake) as a heavy creature package.

resources.name: Weigh All Things to a Nicety

description: Dwar's deck sends Lieutenant of Morgul and a detachment of Orc warriors to Dragon country and to burn a couple Border-holds down. The deck emphasizes large Orc factions and uses Doors of Night to unleash packs of Wolves as hazards.
strategy: Large Orc factions led by Lieutenant of Morgul. Play Burning Rick, Cot and Tree (×2) at Border-holds (Dale, Beorn's House) for burn points. Activate Doors of Night (×3) to unleash wolf hazards (Dire Wolves, Wargs) against the opponent. The Arkenstone + Thror's Map as major items at The Lonely Mountain. Swift Strokes (×3) + Under His Blow (×3) as combat combo. Regiment of Black Crows for extra mobility.

description: Hoarmurath directs a band of Morgul scouts into the fringe Shadow areas of the Misty Mountains to steal technologies and win over independent Orc tribes.
strategy: A scout deck operating in the Shadow fringe zones of the Misty Mountains. Play Records Unread (×3) in Orc-holds (Goblin Gate, Moria, Mount Gram) for knowledge points. Vile Fumes (×3) + War Wolf (×3) as core combat cards. Blasting Fire (×3) for additional striking power. Great Lord of Goblin Gate as a major faction at Goblin Gate. Hazards: Undead chain (Plague of Wights, Ghouls, Stirring Bones, Wisp of Pale Sheen) enabled by The Moon Is Dead + Doors of Night.

description: The Witch-king's mission is to solidify Sauron's forces in Mordor. His minions do best when not moving — from the safety of this evil domain. They have very little to help them tactically, but in Mordor they should not need much. The hazards can create a devastating environment of roadblock.
strategy: Stay in Mordor as much as possible — minimal movement is the key. Score points without travelling using Blasting Fire (×3), That Ain't No Secret (×3), and Great Bats (×3). Vile Fumes (×3) for combat at Mordor sites. Fell Rider + Awaiting the Call for troop assembly. Palantir of Minas Tirith as a major item. Hazards: Long Winter (×3) + Withered Lands (×3) as a devastating roadblock combo against the opponent.

resources.name: Weigh All Things to a Nicety

description: Go to Eagles' Eyrie once you get Smoke in the Wind. Go to the Borderholds when you have Burning Rick, Cot, and Tree. Go to the faction sites when you have neither. Break things. Get points. Win games.
strategy: Three-track approach: (1) Eagles' Eyrie with The Tormented Earth (×3) for environment points. (2) Border-holds with Bold Thrust (×3) for destruction actions. (3) Faction sites for Balchoth, Easterlings, Haradrim, and Corsairs of Rhun. Secret Book (×3) for knowledge marshalling points. Orc Quarrels (×3) for combat support. Hazards: corruption chain (Lure of Expedience/Nature/Senses ×3 each) for heavy pressure on the opponent.

description: A Legendary Hoard deck designed for the two-deck game format. Features a Dragon hazard strategy as natural complement. Perfect for the two-deck game since it requires careful setup over multiple cycles.
strategy: Two-deck format. First cycle: get Wormsbane to protect against your own Dragon manifestation attacks. Pick up factions and ally resources (Iron Hill Dwarves, A Friend or Three). Main goal: set up Legendary Hoard — play the At Home manifestation of Scorba or Agburanar and place Legendary Hoard on it. Use the Ahunt manifestation to rotate the Hoard, but generally save Dragon manifestations to attack opponents who try to plunder your Hoard. Best case: use Uvatha or Mouth of Sauron to play the Ahunt twice in the first deck cycle, rotating Legendary Hoard twice. Second cycle: sideboard in the extra items. The turn before moving to the Legendary Hoard, play the Ahunt manifestation to remove the At Home automatic attack. Then play as many items as fast as possible and leave. If your opponent draws a Slayer: be prepared to face it. Defeat it and you have more time — but always play fast before your opponent can catch up.

description: A Dwarf company under Pallando uses Dragon At Home manifestations to score massive marshalling points via King under the Mountain and Returned Exiles. The hazard mix features Orc creatures and Minion events supported by Doors of Night.
strategy: King under the Mountain strategy. First, play an At Home Dragon manifestation (Bairanax, Earcaraxe, Itangast, or Scorba) on your opponent's turn to establish it at its home site. Then on your turn move there and defeat the automatic-attack, allowing you to play both King under the Mountain and Returned Exiles for large marshalling point bonuses. Durin's Axe and The Old Thrush are essential for defeating the Dragon's automatic-attack. Pallando is the wizard of choice because his ability lets you hold an extra card in play. Blue Mountain Dwarves and Iron Hill Dwarves provide seven influence each; mountain sites add five more. The hazard strategy uses Orc creatures (Lieutenant, Patrol, Warband, Warriors, Watch) plus Minions Stir and The Will of Sauron for event pressure. Hobgoblins and Gothmog supplement as a Minion-themed hazard complement. Adding Dáin II gives an extra body check to secure Dragon kills.

description: Círdan leads an Elven coastal company through the havens and islands of Middle-earth, acquiring resources at Grey Havens, Dol Amroth, Edhellond, Isle of the Dead that Live, and Isle of the Ulond. Three Fellowships, Bounty of the Hoard, and Look More Closely Later drive steady point accumulation. The hazard mix — weather roadblocks (Long Winter, Fell Winter, Snowstorm), drakes, and Shadow of Mordor — locks opponents in place while the company advances along the coast.
strategy: Two cards inspired this deck: Isle of the Ulond and Shadow of Mordor. Your company works the coastal sea, playing resources at Dol Amroth, Edhellond, Grey Havens, Isle of the Dead that Live, Isle of the Ulond, and Tolfalas. Play three Fellowships early to reach Grey Havens quickly and bring Gandalf or Pallando into play. Bounty of the Hoard and Look More Closely Later are the resource engines — Look More Closely Later lets you stack multiple resources at a site well beyond the normal one-per-site limit. Nenseldë the Wingild is your key ally. On the hazard side, Snowstorm, Long Winter, Fell Winter, and Doors of Night form a roadblock that denies opponent movement through Wilderness, while Cave-drakes, True Fire-drakes, and Slayer threaten any company that does push through. Shadow of Mordor targets their resources. Sideboard brings Lure of Power and Morgul-rats for corruption pressure, or Aragorn II and Blue Mountain Dwarves if you need extra muscle.

sites.name: Isle of the Dead that Live
